Ok, so in this particular case if a trial study would be more accurate then I could have just cited one of the studies and said there is no interaction.

The product that meta studies produce, that are useful, but less accurate is when you take additional data taken from responders from one study and compare them with another to attempt isolating more complex interactions. Like, for example, studies that show that napping is sometimes good, and that sleep around 7 hours is good, and using a meta study to validate that cumulative time is what matters. That's useful but might give you a false positive for your theory.
